name: 陳儀
objective: This course deals mainly with the essence of Chinese traditional thought, trying to sovle the riddles lying behind the msytery of Asian philosophy. Through lectures and class discussion, students are expected to have a better command of the significant stream of thinking development for the Chinese people and look into the future cultural development. As for the course planning, this course consists of the following five topics: Pre-Chin philosophers, Taoism in Wei and Jin Dynasties, Buddism in Sui and Tang dynasties, Confucianism in Song and Ming Dynasties and modern philosophy. The course will be presented with simple approaches and lots of class discussions in the hope that  students will realize the wisdom explored by important philosophers throughout Chinese history, which will in returen provide students with much more promising and enrihed way of life.
schedule:

Week 2  Confucius
Week 3  Mencius, Xunzi
Week 4  Teachers’ Day
Week 5  The Logicians
Week 6  Laozi
Week 7  Zhoungzi
Week 8  Retrocession Day Make-up Holiday
Week 9  Presentation Discussion (Students need to give a specific topic of interest for the oral presentation.)
Week 10  School Anniversary Make-up Holiday
Week 11  Hanfeizi
Week 12  Research and Discussion
Week 13  Mozi
Week 14  The Chinese Buddhism
Week 15  Group Presentation 1
Week 16  Group Presentation 2
Week 17  Group Presentation 3
Week 18  Semester Reflection
scorePolicy:
Class Participation and Assignment: 60%
Visit Activity: 10%
Group Presentation: 30%
materials:
JeeLoo Liu (2006). An Introduction to Chinese Philosophy: From Ancient Philosophy to Chinese Buddhism, Blackwell Publishing
Lily Zhang (2011). Thirty Chapters on the History of Chinese Philosophy, Le Jin Books.
Wing-Tsit Chan (1973). A Source Book in Chinese Philosophy, 4th Printing, Princeton University.
I will select some primary Chinese philosophical works as self-made teaching materials. Translations of some texts can also be found online on the Chinese Text Project (https://ctext.org/).
延伸教學與資源: ● 參與式創新教學 (Participatory & Innovative Teaching) 強調學生參與與產出，導入翻轉、PBL/專題、設計思考或遊戲化等策略。Emphasizes student engagement and outcomes by adopting strategies such as Flipped Classroom, PBL (Problem/Project- Based Learning), Design Thinking, or Gamification.

remarks: 1. Confucianism in Week 2-3, Daoism in Week 6-7, egalism in Week 11, and Mohism in Week 13 correspond respectively to SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions), and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities).2. The course develops students’ philosophical thinking through textual analysis and issue-based discussions, with classroom performance used as a measure of learning outcomes. This approach corresponds to the second component of Innovative Character Education, “Explanation.”
